topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This opening frames the lecture's place in the series and introduces its aims for understanding cancer evolution.

topics.label: Mutation-driven clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: The evidence presented explains how successive mutations give cell clones selective advantages during cancer development.

topics.label: Epigenetic disruption in tumor development
topics.groupedBecause: This material examines how altered transcriptional accessibility can drive tumor development without new mutations.

topics.label: Cell of origin and cancer stem cell hierarchies
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how stemness and position within a cellular hierarchy affect a cell's capacity to initiate and propagate cancer.

topics.label: Inflammatory promotion of cancer through acquired stemness
topics.groupedBecause: Both cancer models show how inflammatory signals can confer stem-like properties that allow mutation-bearing cells to form tumors.

topics.label: Stromal dependence of established tumors
topics.groupedBecause: This material connects established tumors' dependence on supportive stromal cells to opportunities for microenvironment-targeted therapy.

topics.label: Single-cell and spatial approaches to studying cancer
topics.groupedBecause: This material explains how molecular profiling of human tissues can reveal tumor evolution and interactions between cell populations.

topics.label: Context-dependent routes to malignancy
topics.groupedBecause: This synthesis explains cancer development as the convergence of cellular fitness and a permissive environment, extending that framework to developmental contexts such as childhood cancer.

topics.label: Lecture close and next session
topics.groupedBecause: This closing ends the lecture and announces the next session on cancer therapy.
